title: Chaplain allegedly fired for posts about marriage files discrimination complaint
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) – First Liberty Institute has filed a religious discrimination complaint with the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) on behalf of a chaplain fired from a Michigan hospice over his religious views. Reverend Richard Blue is an ordained Lutheran minister hired in 2024 to serve as a chaplain at a Heartland Hospice location in Indiana, and in 2026 was transferred to a Michigan facility where he continued to provide spiritual support to patients. … “The discussion on June 22 directly questioned whether my sincerely held Christian beliefs concerning marriage and sexuality disqualified me from adequately caring for patients,” Blue maintains. “I received no additional complaints or reports of misconduct between the June 22 discussion and my termination on July 9. Therefore, I believe that my Facebook posts were the sole cause for my termination. As a result, I believe that Gentiva discriminated against me based on my sincerely held religious “Chaplains should not be forced to give up their religious beliefs to do their job,” said Cliff Martin, senior counsel of First Liberty Institute, which is seeking to have the EEOC open an investigation. “Heartland Hospice cannot single out and terminate an employee for expressing their religious beliefs in their own time and on their own personal social media page.” The Trump administration has tasked the EEOC with affirming religious freedom and pushing back against arguably the most prevalent source of discrimination in corporate America today: woke ideology.
